## _Kay John Yim, London-based CGI artist, explores diverse realms with Marvelous Designer, praising its efficiency and integration in character animation project_

* * *

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9zGa1olQmWo

# **Interview with Kay John Yim | SYMPHONY | CGI Artist**

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

I am a Chartered Architect and CGI Artist based in London, specializing in architectural visualization.

My journey into the realm of 3D began during my time studying architecture at university. In those formative years, CAD software such as Rhino and Revit became indispensable tools of the trade. While I occasionally explored other Digital Content Creation (DCC) software like Modo and Cinema 4D, primarily for rendering purposes, it wasn't until the COVID lockdown in 2020 that I found time to fully immerse myself in the vast world of CG software beyond the realm of CAD. It was during this time that I delved into Houdini, Unreal Engine, ZBrush, and, of course, Marvelous Designer.

Driven by an obsession for creating beautiful imagery, I embarked on a journey to expand my skill set and artistic horizons. I challenged myself to learn and create CG art beyond the scope of my professional work in architecture. This journey led me to explore diverse disciplines such as fashion design, character design, landscape design, and animation, among others. By venturing beyond the boundaries of architecture, I discovered new avenues for artistic expression and uncovered the endless possibilities that CG software has to offer.

This ongoing exploration of various design domains has not only enriched my artistic repertoire but has also broadened my perspective as an architect and CGI artist. It has allowed me to approach architectural visualization with fresh eyes, infusing my work with a diverse range of influences and inspirations.

**BALLERINA**

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HG4yMnx6Tc4

# **Tell us about the project**

"Symphony" celebrates the beauty of ballet. It portrays a ballerina adorned in a pristine white tutu, gracefully dancing within the breathtaking Palace of Venaria. At the culmination of her dance, a synchronized ensemble of ballerinas - each identical in appearance - emerges from behind the window, revealing themselves and captivatingly swaying in perfect symphony.

It unravels a transcendent narrative that explores the interplay between reality and illusion, the nature of identity and collective consciousness.

Although I have previously explored ballet in my personal projects "Ballerina" and "Garnier," "Symphony" stands as my most technically demanding endeavor to date. It showcases an extended character animation and cloth simulation, encompassing the most dynamic movements. Furthermore, "Symphony" represents my inaugural foray into Houdini after transitioning from Cinema4D, presenting an additional layer of challenge in itself.

# **We’d like to hear more about the art direction in costume. What was the visual style you were aiming for?**

While the inception of the costume originated from my previous ballet-themed project, "Ballerina," where I carefully selected a dark fabric adorned with glitters to harmonize with the opulence of baroque architecture, in "Symphony" the intention was to transcend reality into fantasy.

The costume was conceived to seamlessly merge with the pristine backdrop. The choice of a white fabric was deliberate, allowing the costume to elegantly blend into the ethereal ambiance, while simultaneously commanding attention as the focal point within the space. As the animation unfolds, I employed a touch of enchantment, causing her dress to manifest out of the ether, while delicate petals gracefully cascaded from her tutu, evoking an otherworldly sense of magic and wonder.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/e82eaea9deda4a3eb88a584dcc9a7e69/images/f1e0b250cd3f4831a4650c1bd2a8d109230706_4_MD_Screenshot.png)

# **Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer? How did it help you serve art direction?**

Marvelous Designer is very robust in transforming 2D patterns into 3D garments, which stands out among many DCCs I have used for cloth modeling.

It is also one of the fastest for garment simulation I have encountered. While it may not be flawless in certain scenarios, it provides me with a comprehensive overview of the simulation/animation, allowing me to discern areas that require adjustments to produce a better simulation, or design changes in the environment that will better suit the animation, and vice versa.

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline including Marvelous Designer?**

My workflow encompasses several essential stages:

For architectural modeling, I use Rhino for its precision and flexibility.

To bring my CG characters to life, I utilize a combination of Character Creator and iClone. They enable me to create and animate life like characters, capturing their movements and expressions either with built-in tools or additional motion capture equipment. Once I have the animated characters, I then export them into Marvelous Designer for accurate garment fitting and realistic simulation.

In the subsequent stage, I imported all elements into Houdini, where I create the rest of the environment and finishing touches to the imported elements, which includes camera animation, volume interaction (fog), materials, lighting, hair simulation, vellum/FEM muscle/fat simulation and garment simulation cleanup.

Ultimately I used Redshift as my primary render engine for rendering the final animation. I use Neat Video for denoising the final frames, and Magic Bullet Looks for a touch of chromatic aberration and film grain.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/e82eaea9deda4a3eb88a584dcc9a7e69/images/893af80ad44d4c9888d75de5290d9977230706_7_kay-john-yim-thumb-alt0.jpeg)

# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?**

In my initial foray into Marvelous Designer, I primarily relied on the GPU mode for draping and simulation. However, it was through a Marvelous Designer YouTube stream that I discovered the inherent limitations of GPU mode in terms of production readiness. It became apparent that relying solely on GPU acceleration often yielded unrealistic outcomes, marked by bulging garments and peculiar collision behavior. I would therefore recommend fellow Marvelous Designer users to leverage GPU mode solely for garment fitting and draping, reserving CPU mode for the final simulation. By employing this approach, one can strike a balance between efficiency and accuracy.

Through extensive trial and error, I would also recommend one always to set the "Internal" Damping" parameter under "Fabric" > "Property Editor" to 100 when doing cloth simulation, which I find offers the most stable results, significantly reducing glitches and jittering that may arise with the default settings.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Marvelous Designer is unquestionably one of the most intuitive and user-friendly applications I have used. It has seamlessly integrated into my workflow, serving as an indispensable tool for both personal and professional projects, particularly in bringing CG characters to life.

While Marvelous Designer excels in numerous aspects, there are instances where I yearn for more granular control, collision masking being a prime example. Nevertheless, the exceptional speed and efficiency of the software compensate for a lot of the limitations. Its ability to quickly generate realistic cloth simulations has undoubtedly enhanced the efficiency and quality of my work.

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4mOVNr55MvU

by **KAY JOHN YIM**

title: SORCERESS

## _Georgian Avasilcutei, Senior Character Artist, praises Marvelous Designer's efficiency in creating detailed clothing, shares insights, and encourages new users_

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/0e34d69e5b2b4190bbb981dbb2843b94/images/0db819c679734fd29604710ce156448fSORCERESS1.jpg)

# **Interview with**[**Georgian Avasilcutei**](https://www.artstation.com/nimlot)**| SORCERESS | Senior Character Artist / Mentor**

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

Hi. My name is Georgian Avasilcutei. I’m a senior game character artist with more than 20 years of experience in the industry. I’ve worked on quite a lot of games during the years with the last one being Hogwarts Legacy. Nowadays I’m involved less in game production and more focused on my mentorship program, preparing the next generation of artists.

# **When did you start learning Marvelous Designer?**

I have had a fascination for dynamic simulations since the very early days of my 3D career. I was dabbling back in the day with the default cloth simulation in 3ds Max and tried various clothing simulation plugins afterward.

It was a hassle and very time-consuming back in the days but seeing cloth behaving relatively naturally it was so amazing. When CLO 3D evolved into a standalone software I moved instantly to using it. Over the years, even when I was working as a prop artist, I would always choose to simulate fabrics rather than sculpt them, even though at that point the processing power of my pc was not great it was still worth the effort. So I can say I was around Marvelous Designer since the beginning, obviously with more time spent in it once I became a character artist.

# **What model do you want to present to us?**

I’m gonna talk a bit about the sorceress I did some time ago. It was an interesting project in terms of clothing design and I’ve tried to push the usage of Marvelous Designer on more than just the clothing and I think that would be beneficial for the people reading this to see.

For this project I’ve used Marvelous Designer to create obviously the clothing but I’ve also made the book and the scroll pouch on her waist and the boots with the help of Marvelous Designer. People very often disregard how easy it is to create some good leather boots in Marvelous Designer and they prefer to just sculpt the thing and end up with some very unnatural folding most of the time. 

# **How do you start with your design in Marvelous Designer?**

Before doing any actual work of course I need to gather some references. In general, for my personal projects, I went with more design and less following a concept/reference. 

In this case, the base for the clothing was a Chinese traditional dress but to which I added quite a few extra elements to make it belong in a fantasy environment. 

You can see I had in my PureRef quite a few different costumes, concepts and prop inspiration so that I can create something that is unified in design but also unique. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/0e34d69e5b2b4190bbb981dbb2843b94/images/3a907efbfaf24206852020df17d9dc5dsorceress2.jpg)

Once I’ve decided what kind of stuff I want to create is time to prepare the avatar. I know a lot of people who just use the default avatars in Marvelous Designer but I need more control over what I can do. 

People often forget that clothing influences the flesh also so in general you need to make sure that you have sculpted any kind of influence. For example a belt on the waist will deform the flesh and will create some changes in volumes. Sculpting the influence is not only gonna give you a result where the clothing will not just float in place but also the information you need to get some really good folding and a good reference point for where you want a specific piece of clothing to rest. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/0e34d69e5b2b4190bbb981dbb2843b94/images/c21d4108341d4474900e62a917e9d2a9sorceress3.jpg)

You might wonder why I have that “skirt” looking volume on my avatar. The reason for it is that I wanted my skirt to flare but in a very uniform-looking way. Initially, I tried to simulate the skirt using stiff materials but the results would be too far from what I wanted so I decided to give it a helping hand. Especially for games you can use tricks like this because you’re not gonna use this avatar for any animation and you want your model to get as close as possible to the concept/reference without struggling too much. Doing this my skirt ended up quite nice and straight and all the layering fabrics that I have there didn’t prove to be a nightmare when it comes to simulation. 

Due to the fact that most of my work is game art I know for a fact that a lot will be modified afterwards in ZBrush, but in general I try to push my Marvelous Designer work as far as I can in terms of detailing so that when I do corrections in ZBrush they’re all quite small and not require too much sculpting involved. 

As you can see in this image there are still some differences between the final Marvelous Designer result for the clothing and the final high poly in ZBrush. A lot of ornaments, buttons and so on were left to be done outside Marvelous Designer and I haven’t bothered to import them in Marvelous Designer due to their limited influence.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/0e34d69e5b2b4190bbb981dbb2843b94/images/6961374fb8834f1097adc9c3baf3a776sorceress4.jpg)

# **What are the most important things that people ignore when it comes to creating clothing?**

In my opinion, people are not taking care enough about the avatar. From proportions to posture and pose everything counts in the way your cloth will fold. I’ve seen plenty of nice garments fit a very stiff or wrong posture avatar which created some very undesirable folds. When it comes to games it’s quite important to limit the folding in some areas that will deform in a very specific way. There is a reason why I’m always making my clothing in an A-pose even if the final model might end up being in a T-pose for rigging purposes. People also underestimate how much influence the avatar details have. For example, I’ve seen avatars with too low poly density and then the users asking why when they get all that polygon-shaped deformation on their tight-fit clothing. I’ve also seen people who completely disregard the way the cloth influences the flesh and the final result always looks like floating above and not really interacting with the body. 

When it comes to the Marvelous Designer part of things, people have a tendency of ignoring especially the layering effect of clothing. I see people making winter jackets or suit jackets and completely ignore the fact that the clothing has linen. 

If we look at my character at first glance the upper body clothing looks more like a 2 layer job. In reality, I have 4 overlapping layers and the last 2 are also doubled with fabric on the inside also.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/0e34d69e5b2b4190bbb981dbb2843b94/images/2648a26379fc4f338ccee98fc9d2aa56sorceress5.jpg)

Another thing that I’ve seen often is that the users tend to go into detail very soon. It’s a general rule in 3D to gradually add details while making sure that the first pass is as close as possible to what you desire. If you go into details from the beginning you will end up with a nightmare if you want to change a major shape later. So take your time to make sure you have the right fitting for your clothing and that you are in a good place with the way the folds look before adding more poly density and any kind of detail. 

# **Can you do a quick breakdown of the Marvelous Designer work for this character?**

Sure. My character was split into 4 different scenes.

The one you’ve seen in most of the images so far is the main one where I did the dress and scroll pouch. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/0e34d69e5b2b4190bbb981dbb2843b94/images/bc016d448b4c464696c65ffe59dbde86sorceress6.jpg)

The second one is the scene with the boots.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/0e34d69e5b2b4190bbb981dbb2843b94/images/6b1218f9467344cf878bcab80e17438esorceress7.jpg)

**“Why not just model those boots?”**

I’ve got this question during the streams very often and I cannot state how much time I save doing any kind of work in Marvelous Designer. Sculpting good folds requires a lot of experience and precision and even then most of the time you will get it a bit off. Marvelous Designer can help you make leather boots in a matter of minutes. 

I have made a more in-depth explanation about how to approach making boots in Marvelous Designer during one of my [streams.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rl-WtZxESLU&feature=youtu.be)

For the boots, I just wanted some over-the-knee soft leather design that is not too complicated but that brings some interest through nice folding. 

Again the avatar is very important so for the boots I go and sculpt a very simple shape from the leg I have where I collapse the toes into a volume that is very similar to a footwear last.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/0e34d69e5b2b4190bbb981dbb2843b94/images/514bfa943d9747cbbd3cdfd5679872f6sorceress8.jpg)

I draw a quick 3D line on the avatar and flatten it to a shape similar to a sole. This piece will be frozen and used to sew the rest of the boot while getting the nice round shape the leather gets when it’s twisted to connect with the sole. The actual sole was modelled in 3ds Max for these boots.

The third one is the scene for the bracers.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/0e34d69e5b2b4190bbb981dbb2843b94/images/b18452c7e8a2419f853ee7c65652f8bbsorceress9.jpg)

The bracers were a pretty complex shape and I wanted to keep them separated so that I don’t struggle simulating. As you can see I have a lot of rivets and straps that I completely disregard while working in Marvelous Designer. I tend to just put a circle inner line where a rivet would be and just simulate the interaction with the other layers. 

Even though most of the materials on the bracer are very stiff, the slight folding is way easier to achieve here rather than modelling. 

The last one is the scene for the book cover.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/0e34d69e5b2b4190bbb981dbb2843b94/images/f9ccafae84b34cc4807367fbb0020c6csorceress10.jpg)

I wanted to make this book cover and the belts holding it in Marvelous Designer with the intention of making my viewers aware of how easy it is to do stuff like this rather than modelling it. 

As you can see the white patterns are there just to simulate the pages of the book and constrain the cover to a nice shape. As for the rest of the work I did for this character I do not create any kind of buttons or details in Marvelous Designer. My focus is only on making good shapes and having the right folding and interaction. 

You can see in the image that I’ve collapsed all my clothing into a simplified avatar to use as a base for this whole prop. 

# **Do you have anything to say to the new Marvelous Designer users?**

I think the new users need to understand that while Marvelous Designer is a very easy-to-learn software, mastering it requires a lot of experience. Understanding how the patterns behave, learning how to use the internal lines to your benefit, figuring out the fabrics and all the other tools this amazing software provides is gonna take some time and practice. Also, you need to understand that if you want to build some very complex clothing you will need a quite powerful PC.

What I can tell you is that no matter what kind of work you do, you will need to learn how to use Marvelous Designer. At this point there is no better solution to simulate fabrics and the tools in Marvelous Designer are unmatched. Marvelous Designer was and will be one of the most important software in my pipeline.

In the end, I want to thank you for the opportunity to write this and I want to thank the Marvelous Designer team who have been very helpful and supportive in the past years. 

For those interested in the whole process of making this character, the saved videos with the streams while working on this can be found on my [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/nimlot), alongside many other characters that we’ve made during the last years of streaming. 

by GEORGIAN AVASILCUTEI

[Artstation](https://www.artstation.com/nimlot)
content_description: Discover how senior character artist Georgian Avasilcutei leverages Marvelous Designer’s powerful tools to create detailed, realistic clothing and props, sharing expert tips and inspiration for new users.

 _

# **布料制作全流程思路与刚体动态结合分享**

**怒米糠** 老师（B站/A站ID：怒米糠_Unmikang），是一位非常专业的高级建模师，他不仅能创作出非常写实、细节丰富的模型，还非常了解各大软件的长处，并灵活运用它们来完成自己的作品。怒米糠老师还在Bilibili平台上制作教学视频，他的讲课风格风趣幽默，让人听得津津有味又学习到了知识，帮助了很多同学。

# **写实风服装制作流程详解**

 _EA 中国工作室 FIFA wardrobe lead- 马超_

![cb9ec86cbefb43489fdd2023d3a807e7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/46d44484c2184923b3e81c673a72173e/images/cb9ec86cbefb43489fdd2023d3a807e7dded18efcd0f408597a00d392168c610.jpg)

**马超** 老师目前就职于EA，是FIFA Wardrobe的Lead。马超老师负责的项目中需要在Marvelous Designer中制作完成度较高的3D资产，因此积累了大量的项目经验。

在本次用户交流大会中，马超老师将为我们带来非常详细的服装制作技巧分享，由简入繁，先从简单的结构入手，再一步一步修改成复杂的款式。如果你需要在Marvelous Designer中尽可能还原真实服装的多种细节，那一定不要错过本次用户交流大会！

title: Till Death Do Us Part Indeed
content:
## _Visualizing the characters' backstories- their likes, dislikes, occupation, hobbies, etc.- the garment is the most significant part of the storytelling._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/b41b2b949aa5485b9dc51e7b8e7202bf/images/b27acf50c8bb43d8b46d109d5ed6b998till1.gif)

# **Interview with Nishigandha Sahasrabudhe |**[**Till Death Do Us Part Indeed**](https://www.artstation.com/nishigandhasahasrabudhe8)**| 3D Artist**

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

I am a 3D artist based out of Mumbai, India, who loves creating artwork in which the characters have unique little stories to tell. Having graduated in visual design, I started working professionally as a UI/UX designer and simultaneously started dabbling in the world of 3D art. I was always fascinated by 3D animated movies and games from an early age and wondered how the artists brought such breathtaking worlds to life. Soon this awe turned into a strong desire to try illustrating in 3D myself, so I slowly started exploring sculpting objects and characters in various 3D software and have never looked back since. Being self-taught has its challenges, but my love for 3D makes me want to explore and learn something new daily.

# **What inspires you as an artist?**

Visualizing the characters' backstories- their likes, dislikes, occupation, hobbies, etc.- is one of my favorite processes in creating artwork. These backstories shape up the character, quite literally. I sculpt, texture, and light my illustrations, which I enjoy and have fun with. As I mentioned, I love to tell unique stories through my artwork and strive to make my scenes and characters as expressive as possible. I aspire to create art that can be seen, enjoyed, and experienced by all, and that inspires me and keeps me going.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/b41b2b949aa5485b9dc51e7b8e7202bf/images/4bbc60571b1748868405c1c0aa610431till2.jpg)

# **How would you describe your artwork stylistically?**

I want to describe my art as more “stylized” than realistic. Although I like to encapsulate and add real-world details into my pieces, my art style would definitely fall more into the cartoon / stylized domain.

# **What is the story behind the piece?**

This piece is about a beautiful, mysterious woman who charms her lovers and leads them into perfidious situations. I have always wanted to create a villainous character, but I wanted to avoid the obvious visual cues that are generally used to depict a villain or an evil character. So I tried to explore and push the style and tried to depict the corrupt motives of the character using facial form and expressions. Everything about the character, including her beautiful features and gorgeous clothes, contrasts her dark, murderous personality.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/b41b2b949aa5485b9dc51e7b8e7202bf/images/4a18cfb0ff9f44799762dcf264989aa2till3.jpg)

# **What is this character? Are they a part of a larger story?**

Yes, it is a part of a larger story. The main character is a beautiful, mysterious woman who charms her lovers and leads them into perfidious situations. In this one, she is in her wedding gown and looks like someone who has just accomplished what she had set out for. The apple, with the green glow, is a poisoned apple, and the fact that one bite has been taken from it signifies that she has just turned her latest prey into her victim.

# **How does the garment contribute to the storytelling?**

The garment is the most significant part of the story. The witch’s preys are wealthy but asinine men who fall for her beauty and ignore all the warning signs. She feeds off such men to further her wicked motives. Her usual method is, making the men fall head over heels in love with her, marrying her, and then slaughtering them on her wedding night. A poisoned apple is her choice of weapon. The witch is swift and clean and leaves no traces once she has made her kill. The poisoned apple makes it easy and leaves no mess. The beautiful gown conveys that she is either just married or about to get married. The style indicates an older time period. The gorgeous gown shows her sophisticated taste and gives clues about her personality. In this piece with no background, the garment is an excellent indicator to hint at the character and the story.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/b41b2b949aa5485b9dc51e7b8e7202bf/images/31ba9a6d582a4936b43d1f3323c4ee95till4.jpg)

# **Where did you use Marvelous Designer on this piece?**

The complete gown and the veil have been created using Marvelous Designer.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/b41b2b949aa5485b9dc51e7b8e7202bf/images/2fcf11f762df4732ae536d2221acb81dtill5.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/b41b2b949aa5485b9dc51e7b8e7202bf/images/c64efc6c33484bf59e7c0984e0d93306till6.png)

# **Why is Marvelous Designer the best choice for digital apparel creation?**

Marvelous Designer allowed me to experiment with digital clothing patterns and different styles for the outfit. The garment easily forming (from) just 2D patterns helped me visualize how the final piece would look. The cloth simulations helped with capturing the flow of the garment accurately. It’s a very intuitive tool to work with. Creating this garment with any other tool wouldn’t have been so simple.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/b41b2b949aa5485b9dc51e7b8e7202bf/images/dc2b4395e14e457888c13ca985b8c4e8till8.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/b41b2b949aa5485b9dc51e7b8e7202bf/images/60a5dab2491f462eb9c7081ad30719detill9.png)

# **What were the ups & downs in creating this piece?**

I am relatively new to Marvelous Designer software. I have used it before, but not as intensively as in this piece. Figuring out the 2D patterns and stitching the pieces together was one of the process’s most difficult parts since I had minimal sewing knowledge. That was challenging, but seeing your digital garment simulate and drape over your character perfectly was extremely rewarding.

# **Can you share any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer with the community?**

Finalizing the dress design and the pattern and having a clear vision of what design I wanted to go with helped me a lot throughout the process and made the process much faster. The abundant tutorials and videos made available by Marvelous Designer helped me a great deal while creating this piece. Instead of following one tutorial step by step, having a vision and finding answers to questions helps a lot while learning any new tool.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/b41b2b949aa5485b9dc51e7b8e7202bf/images/b1b358d706704ba9b44822dcee73b24ftill10.jpg)

# **What new things did you learn on this project that you might want to share?**

I consider myself relatively new to the software, so I learned a great deal while working on this piece. Learning how to break up the garment correctly into pieces, stitch them up, and how to have fabrics layered one on top of the other without making them interact/collapse into one another is something I learned. Although I did not use this in the end piece, I also learned how to add animation to your avatar and make the garment respond after being draped on the T pose to the final pose of the avatar along with its interaction with the background elements is something I had fun exploring too.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/b41b2b949aa5485b9dc51e7b8e7202bf/images/53856a0e65f548c1ad424789ca0219d9till11.jpg)

# **What were some unexpected outcomes that occurred while working on this?**

I started this piece feeling extremely overwhelmed and intimidated, thinking of the task’s complexity. But the process felt very intuitive, and I enjoyed it more than I thought I would. I started exploring a lot of fashion trends and tweaked my pose and character a bit so it matched and showed off the garment. 

Suppose you're looking for a powerful design software for creating digital garments that's easy to use. Marvelous Designer 12 is perfect for you! It's available on Windows and macOS, and personal licenses are perfect for freelancers or small studios. Enterprise licenses are also available if you're working with a larger team.

title: Death Stranding
content:
## _Check out how Marvelous Desinger's cloth simulation and garment modeling is used in DEATH STRANDING by KOJIMA PRODUCTIONS._

* * *

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EV53lnCzP1w

# **Interview with**[**KOJIMA Productions**](https://www.kojimaproductions.jp/en)**| Death Stranding**

* * *

# **Project Introduction**

Death Stranding is the first completely new title developed by game creator Hideo Kojima since KOJIMA PRODUCTIONS’s establishment. The main character in the game, Sam, does the delivery as a porter in a collapsed world of the near future and connects the citizens who have been separated. There are some elements within the game such as shooting or fighting but yet they are not the main values which make this a very unique type of open-world action game.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/38078041e95b47aa9f1be294add8f924/images/4a2758bf69ee49ca9a09b77839600b8cdeath1.png)

# **How did Marvelous Designer help your project?**

Marvelous Designer and 3D scan-based models were used in half-and-half proportions approximately in the production of Death Stranding's character costume model, fabric in background etc. We also used Marvelous Designer for cloth simulation as well as garment modeling. Not only this but also the skirt, the movement of the blanket, the expressions of the life tube being swollen when entering the water, and the natural movement of the hood when it's being worn by the main character Sam were made out of Marvelous Designer. In the movement of the cape, wind simulations were also used to match the scene.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/38078041e95b47aa9f1be294add8f924/images/ab48f0d6ec63427bb2bd6c1b997cc253death2.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/38078041e95b47aa9f1be294add8f924/images/efef7feec7c64643b68fb56224f08c8fdeath3.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/38078041e95b47aa9f1be294add8f924/images/7cf7a9826dfc460f9859c4121ff44c14death4.png)

# **If there is a memorable expression or production using Marvelous Designer in the project, please introduce to us.**

The shirt Sam wears in the private room is a collaboration with the fashion brand ACRONYM®. Kojima Productions used Marvelous Designer to create in-game assets based on the design that was made by ACRONYM®. Because it is a cloth that exists only in the game, not as a real product, we created its model with the feeling that the designer is making clothes based on ACRONYM®'s design drawings and fabric material samples.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/38078041e95b47aa9f1be294add8f924/images/638174f6599e4a909c6619eac98ee3fbdeatb4.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/38078041e95b47aa9f1be294add8f924/images/2661675d7c2e449b818973b6df2abf5adeath5.png)

# **Please let me know what is the strength of Marvelous Designer compared to other simulation tools.**

In terms of cloth productions, Marvelous Designer is by far superior in the ease of intuitive work, such as pattern making, detailing fitting or sewing settings, and the convenience associated with repetitive work. Also, it is easier to understand and intuitively handle animation than other tools when using it for cloth simulation purposes, so you can keep the animation individually in layers, as well as manipulating the cloth directly in the 3D viewport during the simulation to reflect the animation results. Additionally, it is also great to be able to perform tests repeatedly in a short time since the simulation is light and well responsive.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/38078041e95b47aa9f1be294add8f924/images/da9e0d41f64a46ad88a31db1d4d71f11death6.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/38078041e95b47aa9f1be294add8f924/images/87ff8502454f470180cbcfad1cb8dfd6death7.png)

# **Which features do you want to see from Marvelous Designer in the future version?**

There could be some type of requirements, such as 'alignment with other tools', 'synchronization ON/OFF at any time that supported in the past versions', 'features that do not reset pin or tag settings due to specific editing or avatar replacement', 'Easy to make harder and sharper wrinkles', and 'Conversion of coordinate system during import of Alembic file'. If I run the simulation again after adding or adjusting wrinkles using the Dynamic Wrinkle Brush, the wrinkles I adjusted will disappear. Thus, it would be nice to be able to keep them on another layer or etc. I am also curious to know if simulating tearing fabrics like jeans would be difficult to implement. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/38078041e95b47aa9f1be294add8f924/images/4f681d057c9544b9b581b0be993cfc1cdeath8.png)

# **Would you recommend Marvelous Designer to CG artist and why is that?**

Marvelous Designer allows the intuitive production of patterns and sewing the same as the actual cloth production, which ensures natural and consistent quality regardless of the artist's ability or sense. Of course, there is potential for highly skilled artists to produce better-quality clothes. I highly recommend Marvelous Designer to CG artists.
content_description: Discover how KOJIMA PRODUCTIONS leveraged Marvelous Designer’s advanced cloth simulation and garment modeling to create realistic and dynamic costumes in the game Death Stranding.

My name is Ezgi Yürekli, and I’m a 3D artist working in the game development industry. I graduated from the digital game design department of Bahçeşehir University this year. I love playing games and wanted to be a part of game development. I met with 3D modeling softwares like Maya, zBrush, Marvelous Designer and loved the idea of creating 3D assets for games. I like the aesthetic of stylized art, so I develop myself to create stylized props for games and learn the pipeline of game ready assets in my free time.

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

For this challenge, I decided to use Marvelous Designer mainly. I wanted to create a fringed jacket. I collected my references from a movie called Bronco Billy (1980) and started making the jacket itself. I tried different fabrics to achieve the look that I wanted. The best part of using Marvelous in this project was making the fringes. Marvelous helped me a lot with its physics simulation when it comes to it. It would take a massive amount of time if I were to model them by hand. Also, I can change my avatar to what I want easily, so I didn’t have an issue using the chair that I made for my jacket to hang from. Also, after finishing the jacket I retopologized it inside Marvelous.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/86a72560a51349dc963a760aaf8221b3/images/6a50f35bf14e4543874210f3d65e9ea6jacket2.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/86a72560a51349dc963a760aaf8221b3/images/0b677e62a99d437eb218a1d9a58da1dejacket3.png)

When I first saw Marvelous Designer I loved it because I didn’t see any software like that before. The idea of creating digital clothes with physics simulation sounded awesome. So I jumped right in, tried different tools and I made my first t-shirt. Also I like to discover the softwares by trial and error but sometimes if you want to achieve even a simple thing you have to watch some tutorials. In this case, it didn’t take a lot of time to find my way around Marvelous Designer all by myself. It was so much fun and easy for me to create something, it was like a game to me. I would often open Marvelous and try to do something just for fun. Also Marvelous Designer has really elaborate tutorials too. It is easy to follow and informative. I can easily suggest it if you are looking for tutorials as a new user.

title: Middle Age Dress
content:
## _"Marvelous Designer has enormous potential. I like the different types of fabrics and their different animation! it makes our creations really realistic."_

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/2effd6bc63a14256a0477d2740845d77/images/ea56062081334b62b62fff28e7744babdress1.png)

# **Interview with**[**Manon Devaux**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/LeV1ZK)**| Middle Age Dress | 3D Generalist**

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

My name is Manon Devaux, I am a 3D generalist specializing in clothing. Graduated from the MJM graphic design in Nantes (France). I work today with an Italian advertising company where I model, texture and animate clothes. While learning 3D I fell in love with dress modelling, especially historical. It probably comes from my passion for history and sewing.

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

For this project, I wanted to make a beautiful dress, worthy of a throne room. with embroidery and above all lots of ribbons to make it as realistic as possible. Like all historical clothing, I started with the petticoat and the chemise. They are important so I added details in several places. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/2effd6bc63a14256a0477d2740845d77/images/f6a671886f3042db838dc355198f0acbdress2.png)

I started with a simple pattern (like Mérida in Brave) but added a lot of details: ribbon, gilding, belt, rope, pleated blouse, lace petticoat, etc... The most complicated thing was to play with the layers to that the different linings overlap correctly, especially with the skirt pulled up in one place with a pin. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/2effd6bc63a14256a0477d2740845d77/images/ae8cd15065b041eab705f859f9a642c3dress3.png)

I love long sleeves! It was an obligation for me to do so. But the length of the fabrics and especially the linings was difficult to set up. I had to play with layers and fabrics. I used the standard software avatar. I knew it would only be a "support" for the dress, so I didn't take the time to deal with it. I edited and animated it with Mixamo and Cinema 4D.

It was a great challenge with all those ribbons and carnations! especially the direction of the ribbon (one below one above). I had to play with the fabric, its rigidity and its length (which adapts to the morphology of the character) but I'm happy with the result! 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/2effd6bc63a14256a0477d2740845d77/images/422f6bfce9fb4bb5985de5ea0516bcc3dress4.png)

Above all, in this kind of dress, you must never forget the shirring. They are very important, especially with a slightly transparent fabric like voile. It is the detail that makes the dress more realistic.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

I use this software every day for my work, as well as my personal use and I am very proud of it! Marvelous Designer has enormous potential. I'm sure there are still tools that I don't know about, despite my extensive research online. I like the different types of fabrics and their different animation! it makes our creations really realistic.

title: Lonely Jester
content:
## _"Marvelous Designer is an outstanding and essential software for any 3d artists, not only for clothing creation but also for environment, furniture and props."_

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/7073ab32e3334c01920cc3595f3c6713/images/19ddbcc2729a4d5f9854d941d6be8a17jester1.png)

# **Interview with**[**Elisabetta Sanguineti**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/03VX5G)**| Lonely Jester | 3D Artist**

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

I'm Elisabetta and I'm from Italy. I'm a freelance 3d artist with a focus on digital clothing and accessories. I started approaching digital clothing and 3d props creation 6 years ago as a hobby, but since a couple of years this has become my job. I love contributing to my clients' projects, whether they are video games or short films or commercials. I recently created a profile and store on Artstation to share and compare with other 3d artists.

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

For this project, where the focus was the jester character, I started by creating him. I used Marvelous Designer's standard male avatar, since the character has a mask so I didn't need any special features for his face or hair, I just needed a body with good proportions. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/7073ab32e3334c01920cc3595f3c6713/images/87c4241b58414d74b5284aef5ef69abbjester2.png)

I tried different methods for creating the "puffy" part of sleeves and pants, after a few attempts I fond this shape to have the best result. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/7073ab32e3334c01920cc3595f3c6713/images/1af697444289405f9f341433eb3d69fdjester3.png)

I don't usually model shoes on Marvelous Designer but I wanted to try it and I liked the result. For these, I used leather as the fabric and added some folds in the back with the sculpt tool before exporting.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/7073ab32e3334c01920cc3595f3c6713/images/91f085e0fa814e179844a5e60973d833jester4.png)

Since I knew the character would be sitting, I needed the back of the jacket to be sufficiently attached to the body, and for that, I simply used some tacks. Regarding the hat, to get it in the right position, I used a tack that started from the pointy end of the hat and went to the shoulder, with a thread length of 180mm.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/7073ab32e3334c01920cc3595f3c6713/images/ab1eb25bc8cd49c6af85e8b0f348bba0jester5.png)

After creating the dress in " A pose," I created in Blender a short animation of the avatar from A pose to sitting ( about 25 frames), exported it to alembic format and then imported it into Marvelous Designer to get the final pose. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/7073ab32e3334c01920cc3595f3c6713/images/1142ff6c3816439d8dcda08bd3e7dc5fjester6.png)

The mask, gloves and everything else in the scene were created in Blender, the textures in Substance Painter and the render in Marmoset Toolbag.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/7073ab32e3334c01920cc3595f3c6713/images/6980f2b0c94e4e5cae3acf9ab2575520jester7.png)

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

I use Marvelous Designer literally every day and I think it is an outstanding and essential software for any 3d artists, not only for clothing creation but also for environment, furniture and props. Many file formats are available for import and export, the possibility to integrate Substance materials, the possibility to do retopology, and for example, you can also export the model in.SAMD format, compatible for the Sansar virtual world, you can also find the related Sansar avatars in the Marvelous Designer library. These are some of the features that make it so powerful and so versatile for any pipeline workflow.

One of my favorite things about Marvelous Designer is the ability to create garment animations with excellent quality and realistic simulation for any type of fabric. It is also very important that you can find a lot of tools to learn how to use the software, personally, I have watched tons of videos online and also the discord community is very active!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/7073ab32e3334c01920cc3595f3c6713/images/5d2b3f2b287d4c95aba92eadf2c0de0cjester8.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/7073ab32e3334c01920cc3595f3c6713/images/0e681faed2f241ec8b568b3c979c5a81jester9.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/7073ab32e3334c01920cc3595f3c6713/images/991ccd90f6eb46d1af21f72c225a27bdjester19.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/7073ab32e3334c01920cc3595f3c6713/images/95f1f46a3c0f45eeaaaac10dd716a41bjester11.png)

[**Artstation**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/03VX5G)

[**Instagram**](https://www.instagram.com/__kalis_/)

title: Sisters In Arms -Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six Siege
content:
## _Find out how Marvelous Designer is used in Cinematic Trailer of "TOM CLANCY’S RAINBOW SIX SIEGE"_

* * *

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5tULtBl4lDU

# **Interview with**[**Digic PICTURES**](https://www.digicpictures.com/)**| Sisters In Arms -Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six Siege | CFX Artist**

* * *

# **Introduction: Interviewee Artist & Digic pictures**

I'm Tamás Varga, I work as a character supervisor at Digic. I'm Zoltán Turkovich, Character FX lead at Digic.

# **We’d like to hear more about the art direction of each character in costume. What was the visual style you were aiming for?**

ZT: The film shows the life paths of the two sisters as they work for the Polish counter-terrorism corps JW GROM to take on more and more serious tasks and then join the Rainbow Six team, where they eventually turn against each other because of their increasingly sharp personal differences.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/967cb97bfc8a4b018204e65bc7c2fddf/images/f6b87808214c458587b0f6b58b7075dasister4.jpeg.jpeg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/967cb97bfc8a4b018204e65bc7c2fddf/images/d108b398ed1441b3a1dbfa61a305dbbbsister3.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/967cb97bfc8a4b018204e65bc7c2fddf/images/ab816e1a0f7a4b54885fee98289ce2c9sister1.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/967cb97bfc8a4b018204e65bc7c2fddf/images/c36b1555df91407cab0c1fa4b68c4182sister2.jpeg.jpeg)

We wanted to show their different personalities in Ela and Zofia’s civilian clothes, contrasting the look of the younger brother with a loose denim leather jacket with his sister’s more restrained, elegant style and their father’s funeral uniform.

It was also important that the two raids in the film make it clear to the viewer that they were different events. We also wanted to help with the fact that the gangsters in the harbor wore elegant suits and sweaters, and the criminals running the drug lab in Warsaw were dressed in colorful casual clothes in accordance with the Polish “dresiarz” subculture.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/967cb97bfc8a4b018204e65bc7c2fddf/images/a19b2a9428db4659a46b4cd4b43d81b8sister5.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/967cb97bfc8a4b018204e65bc7c2fddf/images/125356e090c94dc389f1bd405e64ca3asister6.jpeg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/967cb97bfc8a4b018204e65bc7c2fddf/images/5dec4275ca1245d5983bf2069d59f6absister7.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/967cb97bfc8a4b018204e65bc7c2fddf/images/3d668bb30c61467c9eee96203d45f5c5sister9.jpeg)

# **Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer? How did it help you serve art direction?**

We have been working with Marvelous Designer for many years, the first major application of which took place 7 years ago at Witcher 3 - A night to remember.

In our experience, Marvelous Designer is great for shaping the fit, look and dynamic behavior of your clothing in parallel. Another important aspect was that after the costumes were made, we were able to perform the costume simulation work for each shot with this software - so we guaranteed the same results that were approved by the director and art director during the character look development.

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

TZ: Character FX, the body animations made in Maya are transferred to Marvelous Designer as alembic. The dress dynamics setting and the simulation process are done in Marvelous Designer. After the simulation, we run the garment alembic from the Marvelous Designer on a UV basis, combining the rendered garment geometries and finalizing the completed simulations.

# **Could you give examples of some of the iconic scenes and characters Marvelous Designer has been used for?**

TZ: From the Sisters in Arms project, I could highlight criminals in warm-up clothes. One of the most iconic scenes is when the protagonist fights one of the Thug and presses him to the table. For the dynamics of softer warm-up clothes, we were able to achieve very nice results in Marvelous Designer.

# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?**

TZ: What might be useful: The UV-based connection between the render and the Marvelous Designer garment geometries leaves you free to set the performance and shot depending on the Particle Distance within Marvelous Designer.

There are some very good dynamic dynamics presets, they are worth experimenting with, but depending on the performance, they are fine-tuned. Avatar preparation and proper body deformations are important to achieve more realistic dress simulations.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer on the production of Sisters in Arms -Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six Siege?**

TZ: The big advantage is that Marvelous Designer is easy to use and learn, which is why even novice CFX artists quickly learn to use it. In addition to easy operation, detailed parameterization and physically accurate clothing simulations can be easily achieved with the appropriate parameterization. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/967cb97bfc8a4b018204e65bc7c2fddf/images/5aedca37ebad49ccb027e545e2b190b0sister10.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/967cb97bfc8a4b018204e65bc7c2fddf/images/2420f78fb37c4ba0bda61d1975165f83sister11.jpeg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/967cb97bfc8a4b018204e65bc7c2fddf/images/7af41c20732b4829adbd8111df112147sister12.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/967cb97bfc8a4b018204e65bc7c2fddf/images/c077f48ba05e4b7786b141dc166f91b0sister13.jpeg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/967cb97bfc8a4b018204e65bc7c2fddf/images/185e6d53728f484cbed47c38f1bc53bbsister14.jpeg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/967cb97bfc8a4b018204e65bc7c2fddf/images/b34b4db4dd864b60ae518db5f3e7b944sister15.jpeg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/967cb97bfc8a4b018204e65bc7c2fddf/images/b97b2986c9184dabb03547e5533724e3sister16.png.png)

title: Steampunk Sewing Machine
content:
## _"Marvelous Designer is a fantastically powerful software to accomplish different cloth stitching, seams, and sim situations."_

* * *

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HG-CWk2HvbE

# **Interview with Jeremy Scharphorn |**[**Steampunk Sewing Machine**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/8wyEoQ)**| 3D Environment and Prop Artist**

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

Hey! I'm Jeremy and I'm based in the U.S. I am a self-taught 3D Environment and Prop artist. I found out rather quickly that many indie companies combine the roles of a level and environment designer. I had zero ideas how to make anything 3D, but was determined to make any environment I could imagine! Fast-forward a few years and I'm still learning tons in 3D and receiving some game design gigs alongside art ones, but my heart is in environments and props! 

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/24dd2dfa082541eba88fbfbd1aa58644/images/bf7dcb5084dd476394238c4d5de4c45csweing%20machine1.png)

As an environment and prop artist, my cloth needs are a bit different than say, a character artists. As such, Blender has been an alright software for me for these past years since my cloth sim needs have been quite minimal. Though as my skills are going deeper into the intermediate range and as I'm shooting for that coveted "expert" skill set, I am switching to more industry standard tools that pack that extra punch that my work could really use. I'm still rather new to Marvelous Designer and ZBrush, but one rather common pipeline I have seen and am enjoying is using Marvelous Designer for cloth sims and then bringing it into ZBrush for finer sculpting as needed. Though I should confess, with the short time I had left to complete the competition I did skip the ZBrush step and went straight to Substance Painter. The additional fold details were all painted on procedurally with some extra manual adjustments as needed. For a photorealistic piece I would not recommend this route if time permits, but if you're crunched for time like I was, or are doing a stylized piece, skipping the ZBrush step and using Substance Painter is great as well. If I were to do it again I would create everything in Marvelous Designer and refine it as needed in ZBrush.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/24dd2dfa082541eba88fbfbd1aa58644/images/5f80ba749a6847008b8f1eb2d47ca40fsweing%202.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/24dd2dfa082541eba88fbfbd1aa58644/images/842965ed7ba34670ab53ff25eb2e7169sweing%203.png)

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Marvelous designer is a fantastically powerful software. I am constantly surprised while working in it how relatively simple it is to accomplish different cloth stitching, seams, and sim situations. I already knew Marvelous Designer was an amazing software, but when working under that time pressure I was really shown how amazing it can be. Within a few hours, I had exactly what I wanted with no other production experience in the software and certainly no pipeline integration experience with it. Marvelous Designer gave me so much more control than any other software or add-ons could and learning it was incredibly easy! I highly recommend it to anyone, including environment artists, as it just can’t be beat!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/24dd2dfa082541eba88fbfbd1aa58644/images/55c11cdd94fb4fb4a8556db7166c6b21swring%204.png)

by **Jeremy Scharphorn**

## _A 3D Environment Artist, Furkan adapted Marvelous Designer to make a realistic effect with PVC cloth on the table._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/94f8993d0c5049ffbf6be357dcfa6308/images/bb5a8e65382942918fd26571c035f64acyberpunk%20nightclub1.png)

# **Interview with Mehmet Furkan Malli |**[**Cyberpunk Nightclub Storage Props**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/Ar54BN)

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

Hello, my name is Furkan. I’m a 3D Environment Artist working in the game development industry for not so long. I studied architecture in college and it was a pivotal moment for me to realize that I could apply my design knowledge such as form, colour, light and most obviously creating spaces to game art. I have started my game art journey by working on props by interpreting real-life references. Creating multiple props and arranging them in a plausible way was the next step for me, as I have tried to accomplish for this challenge. It’s still an ongoing process for me; creating environments and learning game engines to tell a story. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/94f8993d0c5049ffbf6be357dcfa6308/images/6c038fcf084741619555e93effbcbbb7nighclub2.png.png)

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

After I decide on what to do, I always start with gathering references. I use PureRef to bring together the images I choose. After that, I start to work with blocks and simple geometries. It’s important to see proportions and make it look like how you planned from the beginning. Maya and Blender are my modelling tools for creating low-poly models. Although I could use those tools for high poly, I love how ZBrush can make it easier to create high poly models. In order to bake high poly details to low poly models, Marmoset Toolbag is a very smooth and fast option on my pipeline. For this challenge, I used Marvelous Designer to strengthen the Cyberpunk feeling and overall look. It was easy for me to imagine the cloth and materials when considering Cyberpunk Theme. It was a transparent PVC cloth I had seen on Blade Runner many times, and I knew I could easily simulate and export a single sheet of PVC cloth in Marvelous Designer. After all of these, my favourite part begins which is texturing and Substance Painter, the one and only tool that works for me. Finally to make a portfolio presentation I go back to Marmoset Toolbag for some renders.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

I could say it was an enjoyable and fun process for me. Dragging and pulling the cloth so easily is genuinely entertaining. I could say it was easy to use for me, of course, I’m not creating complex clothing or using it for fashion purposes. However, Marvelous Designer is going to be a great tool for me, as an environment artist, I’m not going to hesitate a second to use it for my scene and won’t bother myself with modelling tools to create cloth pieces. 

by **Mehmet Furkan Malli**

# **An Interview from Monthly 3D Prop Challenge: Leartes Studios X Marvelous Designer - Cyberpunk**

**Learn more about this challenge and be the next special prize winner! (**[**LINK**](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/discover/news/view/115)**)**

* * *

# **1\. Artist Introduction**

My name is Filip Steć. I am a 3D artist with 5 years of experience. I live in Warsaw, Poland and work in the games industry. I usually do environments, but I like trying other things connected with 3D game art. That’s why I participated in Leartes Studios X Marvelous Designer challenge. 

# **2\. Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

I find my pipeline quite standard - for modelling Maya and Blender, for sculpting ZBrush, for texturing Substance Painter, but I see more and more cases where Marvelous Designer can be irreplaceable. Not only in the case of clothes of course, but even in the environment and prop design, it can bring assets to the next level.

# **3\. How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Actually, I find myself a beginner in Marvelous Designer. Before my first try with Marvelous Designer, I thought it’s really powerful but demanding and non-flexible software. I couldn’t be more wrong. In fact, **it’s extremely powerful but I was surprised how I can adjust it to my needs.**

**_by FILIP STEĆ_**
